identity.title: Molecules with ALMA at Planet-forming Scales (MAPS). VI. Distribution of the Small Organics HCN, C<SUB>2</SUB>H, and H<SUB>2</SUB>CO

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present high angular resolution ($10-50$ au) observations of C$_2$H, HCN, and H$_2$CO lines in five protoplanetary disks from the Molecules with ALMA at Planet-forming Scales (MAPS) ALMA Large Program.

The observations are part of the MAPS ALMA Large Program (2018.1.01055.L), where a large number of molecular lines were observed at high spatial resolution to search for links between chemistry and planet formation in protoplanetary disks.

question.value: Characterize the spatial distribution, column densities, and excitation temperatures of the small organic molecules HCN, C2H, and H2CO on planet-forming scales in five protoplanetary disks.

evidence.quote: Small organic molecules, such as C$_2$H, HCN, and H$_2$CO, are tracers of the C, N, and O budget in protoplanetary disks.
Here, we focus on molecular line emission from the small organic molecules HCN, C$_2$H, and H$_2$CO in five nearby and otherwise well-studied protoplanetary disks.

We derive column density and excitation temperature profiles for HCN and C$_2$H, and find that the HCN emission arises in a temperate ($20 - 30$ K) layer in the disk, while C$_2$H is present in relatively warmer ($20-60$ K) layers.

The observations are part of the MAPS ALMA Large Program (2018.1.01055.L), where a large number of molecular lines were observed at high spatial resolution to search for links between chemistry and planet formation in protoplanetary disks.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.01055.L.
Four spectral settings, two in Band 6 and two in Band 3, were observed between 2019 and 2020.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Four spectral settings covering HCN J=3-2 (~265.88 GHz), C2H N=3-2 (~262.00-262.08 GHz), and H2CO 3_03-2_02 (218.222192 GHz) in Band 6; HCN J=1-0 (~88.63 GHz) and C2H N=1-0 (~87.32-87.33 GHz) in Band 3

evidence.quote: The Band 6 setting covered the HCN $J=3-2$, C$_2$H $N=3-2$, and the H$_2$CO $3_{03} - 2_{02}$ lines.
The Band 3 setting covered the HCN $J=1-0$ lines and the C$_2$H $N=1-0$ ladder.
The data include observations using two different array configurations, to provide sufficient dynamic range in baseline length to recover both large-scale and small-scale emission.

angular_resolution.value: 0.15'' (15-24 au) for 3-2 lines; 0.3'' (30-48 au) for 1-0 lines and tapered 3-2 / H2CO lines

evidence.quote: We make use of the fiducial MAPS images, which have a circular beam of 0.15$''$ (corresponding to linear spatial scales of $15-24$ au) for the $3-2$ lines, and a circular beam of 0.3$''$ (corresponding to linear spatial scales of $30-48$ au) for the $1-0$ lines.
For consistency, here we use the tapered version of the H$_2$CO images (with 0.3$''$ resolution) for all sources, which are more sensitive to low surface brightness and extended features.
Four spectral settings, two in Band 6 and two in Band 3, were observed between 2019 and 2020.

analysis_steps.goal: Generate zeroth-moment maps and measure disk-integrated line fluxes

method.value: Integrate velocity channels to create zeroth-moment maps and compute disk-integrated fluxes using elliptical masks based on disk inclination, PA, and observed emission extent.

evidence.quote: For HCN $J=3-2$ and $J=1-0$, all hyperfine lines were included to generate the zeroth-moment maps, while for C$_2$H only the two brightest (and blended) lines are included in the $N=3-2$ line, and the first and brightest component in the $N=1-0$ line.

The fluxes were computed using elliptical masks that were constructed using the disk inclinations and position angles listed in Table 1, and an outer radius based on the observed extent of the emission of each line.

analysis_steps.goal: Extract deprojected radial intensity profiles and radial spectra

method.value: Deproject zeroth-moment maps using GoFish radial_profile and extract Keplerian-shifted deprojected spectra in radial bins of 1/4 beam major axis using GoFish radial_spectra.

evidence.quote: To better characterize the spatial distribution of the emission we used the `radial_profile` function of the Python package `GoFish` (cite: Teague2019) to produce deprojected radial intensity profiles from the zeroth-moment maps, considering the disk inclination and position angle (see Table 1).
To derive column density profiles, we first produce deprojected spectra at different radii using the `radial_spectra` function of `GoFish`.
Before averaging the spectra in each radial bin, the velocity is shifted according to the Keplerian rotation of the disk, so that all the spectra are aligned.

key_parameters.value: Radial bin size = 1/4 of the beam major axis

evidence.quote: The radial bins are set to 1/4 of the beam major axis, and the disk is assumed to be vertically flat.

key_parameters.value: Averaging wedge = 30 degrees along disk major axis (or full azimuthal average for low S/N: C2H in IM Lup and GM Aur, and H2CO in all sources)

evidence.quote: The spectra are azimuthally averaged in those disks with low S/N (C$_2$H for IM Lup and GM Aur, and H$_2$CO for all sources), and averaged within a $30^{\circ}$ wedge along the disk major axis for the others.
The radial bins are set to 1/4 of the beam major axis, and the disk is assumed to be vertically flat.

validation.value: Consistent with lower angular resolution profiles from literature

evidence.quote: The radial profiles are consistent with profiles previously observed at lower angular resolution (0.5$''$) for HCN and C$_2$H in IM Lup, AS 209, HD 163296, and MWC 480 (cite: bergner2019), and for H$_2$CO in all sources (cite: pegues2020).

analysis_steps.goal: Retrieve HCN and C2H column density and excitation temperature profiles

method.value: Two-step LTE hyperfine spectral fitting with thermal line width flux redistribution: first simultaneously fit 0.3'' 1-0 and tapered 3-2 spectra to constrain Tex,0; second fit 0.15'' 3-2 spectra using priors around Tex,0 (and fixed CO temperatures in inner blended regions).

evidence.quote: To derive the column densities, we assume that the emission is in local thermal equilibrium (LTE) and that the emission fills the beam.
First, we fit the $1-0$ and $3-2$ lines simultaneously to obtain a better constraint on the excitation temperature.
In the second step, and to obtain a better-resolved column density profile, we fit the high angular resolution $3-2$ lines only.

key_parameters.value: Free parameters: N_tot, FWHM line width Delta V, excitation temperature T_ex, velocity offset v_lsr

evidence.quote: The free parameters in the fit are the total column density N$_{\rm{tot}}$, the FWHM $\Delta V = 2 \sqrt{2 \ln2} \sigma$, and the excitation temperature in the case of HCN and C$_2$H, as their lines present hyperfine structure.
We also allow for a small offset from the source velocity $v_{lsr}$, constrained between $-$0.25 and 0.25$~\rm{km~s}^{-1}$.

key_parameters.value: Background temperature T_bg fixed to max(continuum brightness temperature, CMB 2.73 K)

evidence.quote: The background temperature $\rm{T}_{\rm{bg}}$ is fixed to the maximum of the continuum brightness temperature or the cosmic microwave background (CMB) temperature (2.73 K).

assumptions.value: Local thermal equilibrium (LTE), beam filling factor of 1, and identical excitation temperature for all hyperfine components

evidence.quote: To derive the column densities, we assume that the emission is in local thermal equilibrium (LTE) and that the emission fills the beam.
We fit the observed spectra assuming that all the hyperfine lines have the same excitation temperature.

assumptions.value: Flux computed with purely thermal line width and redistributed over observed broader line width to account for beam smearing

evidence.quote: A way to alleviate this problem is to first compute the line intensity assuming a purely thermal line width, then compute the total flux, and finally redistribute this flux in the line but now for the observed and broader line width.

fitting.value: MCMC sampling using emcee; Step 1 prior: 10 K < T_ex < T_gas(12CO); Step 2 prior: T_ex,0 - 10 K < T_ex < T_ex,0 + 10 K (or fixed to T_gas(12CO)/T_gas(13CO) in inner disk); velocity offset prior [-0.25, 0.25] km/s; 50th percentile for best fit and 16th/84th percentiles for uncertainties.

evidence.quote: We explore the parameter space using the `emcee` package (cite: Foreman2013). The best fit is taken as the 50th percentile of the samples in the marginalized distributions, and the associated errors are computed from the 16th and 84th percentiles.

We thus restrict the rotational temperature between 10 K and the gas temperature inferred from the peak brightness temperature of the optically thick $^{12}$CO 2–1 line, $\rm{T}_{\rm{gas}}$($^{12}$CO) (cite: law21_surf), for both HCN and C$_2$H.

We used the excitation temperature found in the previous step (T$_{\rm{ex},0}$) as an initial parameter, and constrain $\rm{T}_{\rm{ex},0}- 10$ K $< \rm{T}_{\rm{ex}}<  \rm{T}_{\rm{ex},0}+ 10$ K for both HCN and C$_2$H.

validation.value: Compared against independent HCN retrievals in Bergner et al. (2021) and Cataldi et al. (2021) (including non-LTE fits), finding consistent column density profiles.

evidence.quote: (cite: Cataldi21) performed a non-LTE fit to the HCN lines and found similar column densities, suggesting our LTE assumption is a good approximation, at least for HCN.

An independent retrieval of the HCN column density and excitation temperature is presented in (cite: bergner21) and (cite: Cataldi21), using a method similar to the one presented here but with different constraints on the excitation temperature.

method.value: Fit a single Gaussian to the 0.3'' H2CO 3_03-2_02 line in each radial bin under LTE for fixed excitation temperatures between 20 and 50 K.

evidence.quote: For H$_2$CO, we fit a single Gaussian to the $J=3-2$ line in each radial bin.

Since we only observed one line, the excitation temperature is fixed and the column density was computed for a range of excitation temperatures between 20 and 50 K so that we are not *a priori* assuming the vertical location of the H$_2$CO emitting layer.

findings_qualitative.value: HCN and C2H emission is more compact than H2CO emission by a factor of ~2 and shows rich substructures (rings, central holes, gaps), especially in HD 163296 and MWC 480.

evidence.quote: In general, the HCN and C$_2$H emission is more compact than that of H$_2$CO — their radial extents are smaller by a factor $\sim2$.
The line emission reveals substantial substructure, in particular toward the warmer disks around HD 163296 and MWC 480, where several rings are observed in HCN and C$_2$H.

findings_qualitative.value: HCN emission originates in colder, vertically deeper disk layers (20-30 K) than C2H emission (20-60 K).

evidence.quote: We derive column density and excitation temperature profiles for HCN and C$_2$H, and find that the HCN emission arises in a temperate ($20 - 30$ K) layer in the disk, while C$_2$H is present in relatively warmer ($20-60$ K) layers.
The temperatures are higher for C$_2$H, however, suggesting that the HCN emission arises in a colder and deeper layer than C$_2$H, and is thus more sensitive to density variations.

findings_qualitative.value: There is no universal spatial correlation between millimeter dust gaps and HCN or C2H column density peaks.

evidence.quote: The second column density peak seen at $\sim110$ au toward HD 163296 does not spatially coincide with any of the dust gaps, revealing that there is not a universal connection between dust depletion and C$_2$H or HCN formation.

findings_qualitative.value: H2CO column densities show enhancements near the CO snowline and near the outer edge of the millimeter dust continuum disk.

evidence.quote: The H$_2$CO column densities rise near the location of the CO snowline and/or millimeter dust edge, suggesting an efficient release of H$_2$CO ices in the outer disk.
We find enhanced H$_2$CO column densities at the CO snowline location and another column density enhancement around the millimeter dust edge.

claims.hypothesis: HCN and C2H trace different vertical temperature layers in protoplanetary disks.
claims.experiment: Fit hyperfine structure of 1-0 and 3-2 transitions of HCN and C2H in five MAPS disks under LTE to derive excitation temperature and column density profiles.
claims.result: HCN excitation temperatures are 20-30 K across the sample, whereas C2H excitation temperatures reach 20-60 K, especially in the warmer Herbig Ae disks.
claims.finding: HCN emission arises in colder and vertically deeper disk layers than C2H.

evidence.quote: We derive column density and excitation temperature profiles for HCN and C$_2$H, and find that the HCN emission arises in a temperate ($20 - 30$ K) layer in the disk, while C$_2$H is present in relatively warmer ($20-60$ K) layers.
The temperatures are higher for C$_2$H, however, suggesting that the HCN emission arises in a colder and deeper layer than C$_2$H, and is thus more sensitive to density variations.

claims.hypothesis: Gaps in small organic molecular column densities spatially coincide with proposed forming planets and trace gas depletion.
claims.experiment: Compare high-resolution (0.15'') HCN and C2H column density profiles against proposed planet locations and dust gaps in HD 163296 and MWC 480.
claims.result: A decrease in HCN and C2H column density is found near ~83 au in HD 163296 (where a planet is proposed), and a gap in HCN column density is seen around 70 au in MWC 480 near a dust gap.
claims.finding: HCN (and C2H in HD 163296) shows column density depletions at proposed planet locations and can trace gas density perturbations.

evidence.quote: In the case of HD 163296, we find a decrease in column density for HCN and C$_2$H inside one of the dust gaps near $\sim83$ au, where a planet has been proposed to be located.

If there is a corresponding gas gap, then this suggests that HCN may be more sensitive to gas density perturbations than C$_2$H, and could potentially be used as a diagnostic to identify massive planets in protoplanetary disks.
HD 163296 and MWC 480 show gaps in their HCN column density profiles, which spatially coincide with the location of planets suggested in previous studies.

claims.hypothesis: Enhanced UV penetration inside millimeter dust gaps universally drives enhanced photochemistry and column density peaks of HCN and C2H.
claims.experiment: Compare radial locations of HCN and C2H column density peaks with resolved millimeter dust continuum gaps.
claims.result: While innermost C2H peaks in several disks align with inner dust gaps, other peaks (such as the ~110 au peak in HD 163296) do not coincide with any dust gap.
claims.finding: There is no universal connection between millimeter dust depletion in gaps and HCN or C2H column density enhancements.

evidence.quote: The second column density peak seen at $\sim110$ au toward HD 163296 does not spatially coincide with any of the dust gaps, revealing that there is not a universal connection between dust depletion and C$_2$H or HCN formation.

claims.hypothesis: Outer-disk H2CO emission is linked to grain-surface formation via CO hydrogenation and ice desorption at the millimeter dust edge.
claims.experiment: Derive radial column density profiles of H2CO 3_03-2_02 and compare substructure locations with the CO snowline and millimeter dust continuum outer edge.
claims.result: First H2CO rings in HD 163296 and MWC 480 coincide with the CO snowline, and outer rings/shoulders in HD 163296, MWC 480, IM Lup, and GM Aur coincide with the millimeter dust edge.
claims.finding: CO hydrogenation on grains and efficient ice desorption near the millimeter dust edge significantly contribute to outer disk H2CO gas.

evidence.quote: The first H$_2$CO ring seen toward HD 163296 and MWC 480 spatially coincides with the estimated location of the CO snowline, suggesting that CO hydrogenation is an important (if not dominant) formation pathway of H$_2$CO in disks.
In particular, the second ring or bump component seen in the H$_2$CO column density profiles of HD 163296 and MWC 480 spatially coincides with the millimeter dust edge.
The H$_2$CO column densities rise near the location of the CO snowline and/or millimeter dust edge, suggesting an efficient release of H$_2$CO ices in the outer disk.

claims.hypothesis: The inner 50 au planet-forming regions of protoplanetary disks contain an organic reservoir comparable to Solar System comets.
claims.experiment: Integrate gas column densities within 50 au, apply an ice-to-gas ratio of 1000, and compare to modeled water ice masses within 50 au.
claims.result: Total gas+ice organic masses in the inner 50 au are 10^23 - 10^26 g, with abundances relative to water ice (0.5%-1.1% for HCN, 0.02%-1.8% for C2H, 0.001%-0.08% for H2CO, excluding IM Lup) similar to cometary values.
claims.finding: Inner 50 au regions are rich in organics, and comets formed in these disks could deliver water and organics to rocky planets.

evidence.quote: Finally, we find that the inner $50$ au of these disks are rich in organic species, with abundances relative to water that are similar to cometary values.

evidence.loc: Small organics reservoir in the inner 50 au
evidence.quote: Typical abundances with respect to water in cometary ices range from 0.1% to 0.6% for HCN and from $0.1-1\%$ for H$_2$CO (cite: mumma2011), which are consistent with our organic fraction estimates.

why_this_data.value: Provides high angular resolution (0.15''-0.3'', 10-50 au) and high brightness sensitivity across both 1-0 (Band 3) and 3-2 (Band 6) transitions to resolve chemical substructures and constrain excitation temperatures.

evidence.quote: The MAPS data presented in this paper provide a combination of high angular resolution with excellent brightness sensitivity, which enables us to identify substructure in the line emission of these small organics.

evidence.loc: Location of the HCN and C$_2$H emission surfaces
evidence.quote: In addition, the $1-0$ line observations now allow us to better constrain the molecular excitation temperature.

why_this_method.value: Deprojecting within a 30 degree wedge along the major axis avoids emission surface height uncertainties; thermal line width flux redistribution mitigates beam smearing in hyperfine fits; two-step fitting combines multi-band Tex constraints with 0.15'' spatial resolution.

evidence.quote: The main motivation for using a $30^{\circ}$ wedge when possible is to avoid the uncertainty of the emission surface height, which strongly influences the spatial location of emission near the minor axis.

A way to alleviate this problem is to first compute the line intensity assuming a purely thermal line width, then compute the total flux, and finally redistribute this flux in the line but now for the observed and broader line width.
First, we fit the $1-0$ and $3-2$ lines simultaneously to obtain a better constraint on the excitation temperature.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Taking vertical emission height into account when deriving radial profiles (rejected in favor of a flat disk assumption with a 30 degree major-axis wedge).

evidence.quote: Although it is possible to take into account the vertical height of the emission to derive the radial intensity profiles (cite: law21_rad), here we assume a flat disk but produce the deprojected profiles by averaging the emission within a $30^{\circ}$ wedge along the disk major axis.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using 0.15'' resolution H2CO images (rejected in favor of 0.3'' tapered images for all sources due to low S/N at 0.15'' except in GM Aur).

evidence.quote: For consistency, here we use the tapered version of the H$_2$CO images (with 0.3$''$ resolution) for all sources, which are more sensitive to low surface brightness and extended features.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using T_gas(12CO) as the fixed inner-disk excitation temperature for HCN in Herbig Ae disks (rejected in favor of T_gas(13CO) because 12CO produced a large column density discontinuity).

evidence.quote: For the two disks around Herbig Ae stars, however, the $\rm{T}_{\rm{gas}}$($^{13}$CO) was used instead, since the $\rm{T}_{\rm{gas}}$($^{12}$CO) produced a large discontinuity in the column density profile.

limitations_admitted.value: Spectral line fits perform poorly in the inner disk (<30 au) where lines are broadened by beam smearing and back-side contamination, completely blending hyperfine components.

evidence.quote: The lines are fit well in most of the disk, but poorly fit in the inner disk, where the lines are substantially broader, resulting in the individual hyperfine components being completely blended.

As was found for HCN and C$_2$H, the lines are fit well in most of the disk, but poorly fit in the inner $\sim30$ au, especially in HD 163296 and MWC 480. This is probably due to contamination from the back side of the disk.

limitations_admitted.value: Only a single H2CO transition was observed, preventing a direct constraint on the H2CO excitation temperature.

evidence.quote: Since we only observed one line, the excitation temperature is fixed and the column density was computed for a range of excitation temperatures between 20 and 50 K so that we are not *a priori* assuming the vertical location of the H$_2$CO emitting layer.

limitations_admitted.value: Inner 50 au HCN masses for GM Aur, HD 163296, and MWC 480 may be underestimated due to inward constant-column-density extrapolation.

evidence.loc: Small organics reservoir in the inner 50 au
evidence.quote: This means that the HCN masses estimated for GM Aur, HD 163296, and MWC 480, which tend to have centrally peaked N profiles, could be larger than what we have estimated here.

referee_caveats_inferred: Total gas+ice organic masses and water-relative abundances in the inner 50 au rely on an assumed uniform ice-to-gas ratio of 1000 and inward extrapolation where lines are optically thick/blended.
Assuming a flat disk geometry during radial spectral extraction may introduce minor radial smearing for elevated layers, even within a 30 degree wedge.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Tens of GB for the released image cubes (5 disks x 5 line setups at 0.15'' and 0.3''); several TB if reprocessing raw visibilities from 2018.1.01055.L.
reproducibility.score_reason: High-level science products (image cubes, moment maps) are publicly hosted by the MAPS team, spectroscopic constants and equations are explicitly given in the text, and open-source tools (GoFish, emcee) are used, though the custom hyperfine fitting script and exact inner-disk cutoff radii are not provided.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The calibrated/imaged ALMA data cubes are publicly available, the radial extraction and LTE radiative transfer equations are fully specified, and key quantitative outputs (integrated line fluxes in Table 4, inner 50 au masses in Table 3, and column density/Tex profiles) provide clear numerical benchmarks.
